source_note: Mechanism / aggregation pathology failure modes for the L5 layer (METHODOLOGY.md §5d). Distinct from the other taxonomies: L1-L3 (cognitive_biases.json) record properties of judgment; L4 (strategic_failure_modes.json) records actor-level incentive misalignment; L5 records pathologies of the aggregation mechanism itself — outcomes that no individual actor selected and that would persist even under informed, good-faith participation, because the mechanism class has a documented constraint. Theoretical bases: social choice theory (Arrow 1951, Gibbard 1973, Satterthwaite 1975, Sen 1970, Condorcet); algorithmic game theory and price-of-anarchy (Koutsoupias-Papadimitriou 1999, Roughgarden 2005); common-pool / collective action (Hardin 1968, Olson 1965, Ostrom 1990); transaction-cost economics (Coase 1937, 1960; Williamson 1975, 1985); agenda-control / multidimensional voting (Plott 1967, McKelvey 1976, Schofield 1978); federalism and jurisdictional mismatch (Oates 1972, Weingast 1995); Schelling brinkmanship and deadlock (Schelling 1960, 1966). Validity of any L5 entry requires all four of S1-S4 (METHODOLOGY.md §5d). Each entry carries an 'operational_signature' — the documentary pattern the Failure-Mode Classifier looks for. The 'subtype' field maps to the L5 sub-types in §5d.

subtypes.L5a: Social-choice impossibility — aggregation rule hit a documented impossibility / cycling / strategic-manipulation result (Arrow, Condorcet, Gibbard-Satterthwaite, Sen).
subtypes.L5b: Price-of-anarchy gap — individually rational Nash play produces a collectively inferior outcome; gap to a Pareto-reachable equilibrium is documented.
subtypes.L5c: Common-pool / collective-action failure — Hardin/Olson structure; no Ostrom-style enforcement institution invoked despite known availability.
subtypes.L5d: Transaction-cost veto — Pareto-improving move exists but transaction costs exceed private gain for every would-be mover; alternative low-cost mechanism documented in analogous setting.
subtypes.L5e: Agenda control / cycling — Plott-McKelvey; output determined by ordering of votes / motions / amendments rather than by preferences.
subtypes.L5f: Jurisdictional mismatch — scope of the decision mechanism does not cover the scope of the externality; a cross-jurisdiction institution is known in analogous settings but was not invoked.
subtypes.L5g: Temporal compounding / oscillation — sequence of locally rational moves produces a trajectory no actor chose as a goal; or a decision oscillates without new information reaching the decider.
subtypes.L5h: Deadlock / brinkmanship equilibrium — mutual veto or mutual threat produces a lose-lose stable point; a documented tie-break / mediation channel existed and was not used.

modes.name: Arrow-applicable aggregation hit impossibility constraint
modes.definition: The decision used a preference-aggregation rule over a domain where the conditions of Arrow's theorem (universal domain, non-dictatorship, independence of irrelevant alternatives, Pareto, transitivity) apply, and the observed output exhibits one of the forced violations. No alternative rule that could have been used in the same body (e.g. score voting, approval, pairwise with documented tie-break) was considered on the record.
modes.operational_signature: Three or more alternatives, multi-dimensional preferences documented; outcome is order-sensitive or non-Pareto; the body has procedural latitude on rule choice; no deliberation on alternative rules appears in the record.

modes.name: Condorcet cycle in pairwise voting
modes.definition: A body used sequential pairwise elimination or amendment votes over options whose pairwise preference structure contains a documented cycle (A beats B, B beats C, C beats A among the voters). The chosen option is therefore an artifact of which pairing was scheduled first, not of aggregate preference.
modes.operational_signature: Voting transcripts allow reconstruction of pairwise preferences; a cycle exists; the eliminated options in earlier rounds would have beaten the winner had the schedule differed; schedule rationale not documented.

modes.name: Gibbard-Satterthwaite strategic misrepresentation determining outcome
modes.definition: The voting / bidding / amendment rule is non-dictatorial with ≥3 outcomes; documented strategic voting (voters misrepresenting preferences to affect the outcome) shifted the result. The body had access to strategy-proof alternatives (randomization, restricted domain, approval with documented cut-off) and did not invoke them.
modes.operational_signature: Post-vote testimony, leaked positions, or inconsistency between public reasoning and vote reveal strategic misrepresentation; the pivot caused by the strategic votes changes the outcome on the record; no strategy-proofing of the mechanism is documented.

modes.name: Nash equilibrium with documented Pareto gap
modes.definition: Agents with aligned information reach a Nash equilibrium whose payoff-profile is Pareto-dominated by another reachable profile. No coordination, communication, or commitment mechanism (which would move the game off the individually-rational frontier) was attempted despite documented availability.
modes.operational_signature: Payoff structure is reconstructable from public records (budgets, regulations, official incentive schedules); the better equilibrium is documented in analogous settings; the cost of the coordination mechanism is lower than the gap; no attempt is on the record.

modes.name: Plott-McKelvey agenda control in multidimensional space
modes.definition: A multidimensional policy decision was resolved by majority rule through a specific sequence of amendments or motions. Documentable alternative orderings of the same amendments would have yielded substantively different outputs. The agenda-setter is identifiable and the ordering was not justified substantively.
modes.operational_signature: Policy space is multi-dimensional (≥2 independent issue axes); amendment / motion sequence is recorded; a plausible alternative sequence exists in the body's own procedural history; the rationale for the chosen sequence is procedural, not substantive.

modes.name: Hardin common-pool collapse without enforcement institution
modes.definition: A shared resource (fishery, aquifer, airshed, spectrum, fiscal commons, administrative capacity) is governed under open-access or nominal-rights conditions; exploitation exceeds regeneration; no sanction / quota / assignment mechanism is operationally enforced. Ostrom-style governance (graduated sanctions, nested enterprises, monitoring by users) is documented in analogous commons but was not adopted.
modes.operational_signature: Resource depletion / congestion is measured in official data; the governing body has rule-making authority over the commons; no enforced allocation or sanction mechanism is on the record; analogous commons with documented governance produce sustained resource flows.

modes.name: Olson-type large-group public-good failure
modes.definition: A public good with diffuse beneficiaries and concentrated opposition is not provided. The beneficiary group lacks selective incentives to organize (Olson); the opposition is small-enough to organize. No mechanism to solve the selective-incentive problem (matched funding, user fees, automatic contribution, statutory provision) is on the record.
modes.operational_signature: Benefit distribution is diffuse and well-documented; cost distribution is concentrated and well-documented; organized lobbying record is one-sided; available institutional responses (automatic provision, opt-out contribution, earmarked revenue) were considered and rejected without engagement with the selective-incentive problem, or were not considered at all.

modes.name: Coase-Williamson transaction-cost veto of Pareto move
modes.definition: A Pareto-improving reallocation is theoretically available but is not made because transaction costs (negotiation, enforcement, contingent contracting) exceed the private gain to any party able to initiate. A documented low-transaction-cost alternative mechanism (a clearinghouse, a statutory default, a single-price auction) exists in analogous settings.
modes.operational_signature: The better allocation is identifiable in official analyses; the transaction-cost source is nameable (number of parties, legal uncertainty, enforcement asymmetry); the mover most able to initiate has no private residual claim that would justify the cost; a documented low-cost mechanism exists and was not attempted.

modes.name: Jurisdictional-scope / externality-scope mismatch
modes.definition: The decision mechanism covers a smaller geographic / functional / temporal scope than the externality of the decision. No cross-jurisdiction coordination body with authority over the externality is invoked, although one exists in analogous settings (interstate compact, international convention, cross-ministry council, generational-impact board).
modes.operational_signature: The externality's scope is documented (emissions, capital flows, epidemiological transmission, long-horizon obligations); the deciding body's scope is smaller; a cross-jurisdiction institution with formal authority on the same class of question exists elsewhere and is not invoked; the decision rationale treats the out-of-scope externality as out-of-concern.

modes.name: Concurrent-jurisdiction conflict without coordination
modes.definition: Two or more bodies have overlapping authority on the same question; their decisions conflict or one pre-empts the other without a coordination mechanism being invoked. An available coordination channel (joint committee, memorandum of understanding, statutory primacy clause, mediation panel) is documented in the body's own institutional framework and is not used.
modes.operational_signature: Conflicting rules / rulings from bodies with overlapping jurisdiction exist on the record; the conflict is documentable in reporting or litigation; the coordination mechanism is in published procedure and was not invoked; the final outcome is determined by timing, political weight, or resource asymmetry rather than by substantive resolution.

modes.name: Temporal-discount trajectory of locally rational moves
modes.definition: A sequence of decisions, each defensible under the discount rate applied to its specific window, produces a cumulative trajectory that no actor in the sequence would have chosen as an end-state. The discount rate used at step-level exceeds the rate implied by the mandate's long-horizon obligations; no long-horizon check mechanism (multi-year budget review, generational-impact board, sunset clause with mandatory review) is invoked.
modes.operational_signature: Each decision in the sequence is documentably justified at its own time; the cumulative state at T+n is documentable in ex-post analyses; the delta between step-level discount rate and mandate-level discount rate is quantifiable or qualitatively clear; no cumulative-state review was scheduled or conducted during the sequence.

modes.name: Oscillation without new information
modes.definition: A body reverses its decision on the same matter two or more times within a window during which no material new information entered the decision-relevant record. The reversals track composition change, political cycle, or agenda-rotation rather than evidence. The body has a standing-decision or res-judicata mechanism that could stabilize the ruling and did not invoke it.
modes.operational_signature: ≥2 reversals on a matter within a bounded window; information environment unchanged per the body's own working record; reversal timing correlates with composition / cycle / agenda rather than evidence; standing-decision / precedent mechanism exists in the body's procedure and was not invoked.

modes.name: Schelling deadlock / mutual-veto equilibrium
modes.definition: Two or more veto-holders occupy positions such that any move toward agreement by one is exploited by the other; a stable lose-lose equilibrium forms. A documented mediation / tie-break / commitment-device mechanism (binding arbitration, sunset with automatic default, credible third party) is available in the body's framework and is not invoked.
modes.operational_signature: Multiple veto-points documented; each side's public position shifts are followed by the other's extraction attempts documented in contemporaneous record; the mediation mechanism is in published procedure; cost of continued deadlock exceeds the cost of the mediation mechanism for all parties per reconstructable analysis.

modes.name: Procedural-parity stalemate without tie-break
modes.definition: A bicameral, multi-chamber, or multi-veto system produces a null output on a matter whose decision is mandated by schedule or statute. A documented tie-break channel (conference committee, casting vote, cross-chamber reconciliation, escalation to higher body, referendum) exists in the constitutional or procedural framework and is not invoked or is invoked after the mandate window has closed.
modes.operational_signature: Mandated decision window has closed with no output; tie-break channel is explicit in published procedure; the channel was not used or was used past the window; the absence of decision has foreseeable downstream cost documented in pre-window analyses.
